scenes.tts: Two findings both end with a mouse not breathing. Are they the same line, used twice?
scenes.visual: Title card: Two Ways to Stop Breathing. Two arrows from different starting points converge on one suppressed breathing trace, with a question mark above.
scenes.narration: Two findings both end with a mouse not breathing. Are they the same line, used twice?

scenes.tts: Start with the opposite results. Light on P two R Y one afferents suppressed breathing in anaesthetized mice.
scenes.caption: Start with the opposite results. Light on P2ry1 afferents suppressed breathing in anaesthetized mice.
scenes.visual: Left panel of the optogenetics setup: an exposed nerve under a thin light fibre, gold P2ry1 axons lit, breathing trace suppressed.
scenes.narration: Start with the opposite results. Light on P2ry1 afferents suppressed breathing in anaesthetized mice.

scenes.tts: Light on N P Y two R afferents produced rapid shallow breathing. Opposite outputs, in the same nerve.
scenes.caption: Light on Npy2r afferents produced rapid shallow breathing. Opposite outputs, in the same nerve.
scenes.visual: Right panel, matched composition: gold Npy2r axons lit, breathing trace rapid and shallow. Both panels now side by side.
scenes.narration: Light on Npy2r afferents produced rapid shallow breathing. Opposite outputs, in the same nerve.

scenes.tts: This is sufficiency. It says what each population can do when driven, not what drives it in life.
scenes.visual: A label over both panels: sufficiency, driven with light. Below: natural stimulus, unknown here.
scenes.narration: This is sufficiency. It says what each population can do when driven, not what drives it in life.

scenes.tts: Nerve recordings added an independent check. One population was mostly fast, the other mostly slow.
scenes.visual: Two axon cross-sections: one wrapped in myelin, one bare. A speed bar beside each.
scenes.narration: Nerve recordings added an independent check. One population was mostly fast, the other mostly slow.

scenes.tts: A fibres are myelinated and conduct quickly. C fibres are unmyelinated and conduct slowly.
scenes.visual: Labels appear: A fibre, myelinated, fast; C fibre, unmyelinated, slow. P2ry1 tagged largely A fibre, Npy2r largely C fibre.
scenes.narration: A fibres are myelinated and conduct quickly. C fibres are unmyelinated and conduct slowly.

scenes.tts: Conduction speed was measured apart from the breathing assay. Most of one population conducted fast, most of the other slow. That is a physiological difference, not proof of complete separation.
scenes.visual: A recording symbol linked to the labelled axons, with a speed bar beside each axon type. Labels: predominantly A fibres, predominantly C fibres. No crossed arrow.
scenes.narration: Conduction speed was measured apart from the breathing assay. Most of one population conducted fast, most of the other slow. That is a physiological difference, not proof of complete separation.

scenes.tts: Now the two routes to one output. First, inflation. When the lungs fill, further inspiration is cut short.
scenes.visual: A lung inflating; the breathing trace shows inspiration ending early. Label: inflation, stimulus is stretch.
scenes.narration: Now the two routes to one output. First, inflation. When the lungs fill, further inspiration is cut short.

scenes.tts: This is the Hering-Breuer inflation reflex, described more than a century ago. Cut both vagi and the reflex goes.
scenes.visual: Label: Hering-Breuer inflation reflex. Two panels during the same sustained inflation. Left: intact pulmonary vagal input, with inspiration interrupted. Right: both vagi interrupted, with the interruption gone. Caption: inflation-reflex feedback absent. The right trace is not labelled normal.
scenes.narration: This is the Hering-Breuer inflation reflex, described more than a century ago. Cut both vagi and the reflex goes.

scenes.tts: Second, protection. Water or acid at the larynx triggers protective reflexes that keep the airway clear.
scenes.visual: A larynx with a drop of water and a drop of acid. Label: protection reflex, evoked by an irritant, not by lung stretch. Caption: which afferents sense it is a separate measurement.
scenes.narration: Second, protection. Water or acid at the larynx triggers protective reflexes that keep the airway clear.

scenes.tts: Driving P two R Y one afferents with light recruited the whole program, not apnoea alone.
scenes.caption: Driving P2ry1 afferents with light recruited the whole program, not apnoea alone.
scenes.visual: A list builds: apnoea, closure of the vocal folds, swallowing, expiratory reflexes.
scenes.narration: Driving P2ry1 afferents with light recruited the whole program, not apnoea alone.

scenes.tts: Ablating those cells impaired swallowing to laryngeal water and acid. That is necessity, in that assay.
scenes.visual: The labelled cells fade out of the ganglion; the swallowing row of the list dims. Label: necessity, that assay, that age, that driver.
scenes.narration: Ablating those cells impaired swallowing to laryngeal water and acid. That is necessity, in that assay.

scenes.tts: So these cells can recruit airway defence, and one tested piece of it needs them. Predict. If they were also the lung's stretch detector, what would inflation imaging show?
scenes.visual: A ganglion field drawn with blank cells, an inflation cuff on the airway, and a question: which cells light up, and what label do they carry?
scenes.narration: So these cells can recruit airway defence, and one tested piece of it needs them. Predict. If they were also the lung's stretch detector, what would inflation imaging show?

scenes.tts: If one population did both jobs, the inflation responders should sit inside the labelled set.
scenes.visual: Inflation-responsive cells drawn as a subset within the larger labelled set. Caption: if these responders belong to the P2RY1-labelled population, they should carry that label.
scenes.narration: If one population did both jobs, the inflation responders should sit inside the labelled set.

scenes.tts: They did not. Most stretch-responsive neurons were Piezo two positive and P two R Y one negative.
scenes.caption: They did not. Most stretch-responsive neurons were PIEZO2-positive and P2RY1-negative.
scenes.visual: The real result: lit cells in the ganglion field, with the P2RY1 overlay failing to match them. Labels: PIEZO2-positive, P2RY1-negative.
scenes.narration: They did not. Most stretch-responsive neurons were PIEZO2-positive and P2RY1-negative.

scenes.tts: That imaging was done with central connections severed, under isoflurane, with the airway inflated in the living animal.
scenes.visual: The preparation drawn plainly: ganglion imaged, central connections cut, anaesthetic label, airway inflation in vivo.
scenes.narration: That imaging was done with central connections severed, under isoflurane, with the airway inflated in the living animal.

scenes.tts: So two populations, two challenges, one shared output. The table separates them.
scenes.visual: Two-column table builds: protection afferents versus stretch afferents. Rows for the challenge used to evoke the reflex, handle, output when driven, cell-ablation result, and channel-loss result. The challenge row notes that P2ry1-cell ablation tests a contribution to the reflex, not direct water or acid transduction, and that inflation-responsive afferents were imaged. The channel-loss row gives P2X2/P2X3 double loss for protection, marked as not a P2ry1-cell-specific deletion, and adult sensory-neuron Piezo2 deletion for stretch. The two interventions are labelled separately with their population scopes written out.
scenes.narration: So two populations, two challenges, one shared output. The table separates them.

scenes.tts: The takeaway is general. An output alone does not identify which pathway produced it. Measure stimulus and output separately.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: two different challenges, two different populations, one output. Caption: an output alone does not identify a pathway.
scenes.narration: The takeaway is general. An output alone does not identify which pathway produced it. Measure stimulus and output separately.
